promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Great first week: three runs, no pain. Keep to three runs again, slow the running parts to an easy effort, and add only a few minutes.

flags.title: Running effort too high
flags.detail: Effort was 6-7/10 and about a quarter of your time sat in zone 3. Slow the running parts until you can talk in full sentences, with heart rate under 135.

flags.title: Calf tightness
flags.detail: Tight the day after a run and gone by morning fits a new runner. If it lingers into your next run, turns sharp or stays on one side, stop running and see a physio.

flags.title: No back-to-back runs
flags.detail: Keep Tue, Thu, Fri and Sun free of running. Your legs adapt on the rest days, and the dog walks are enough movement.

flags.title: Small step up only
flags.detail: Total time goes from 64 min to 69 min. Do not add extra on days you feel good, because new runners get hurt by doing too much too soon.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer:
No, keep to three runs a week. Running every day would add far more load than your calves and shins are ready for, and your calves are already tight the day after each run.

You get fitter during the rest between runs, not during the runs themselves. Ten weeks is enough time to build up to running the whole 5K if you stay consistent with Monday, Wednesday and Saturday and don't get injured.

new.analysis:
Your first week went well. You ran all three planned mornings with no pain, and the longest run grew from session to session. This week repeats that pattern with a small step up, and the main change is how hard the running parts feel.

The running parts were a little too hard. Effort 6-7/10 and 27% of your time in zone 3 is more than a walk-run needs at this stage. Easy running builds your heart, lungs and the tendons and bones that take longer to adapt than your muscles. If every session feels like work, you risk tiring out or getting sore before the fitness arrives. Slowing down now makes it easier to run for longer later.

Your calves are tight the day after each run and clear by the next morning. That is a common response when legs take on new load, so it is not a worry yet. It is the first thing to watch if you add too much too fast, which is another reason to hold at three runs.

"Build" for you does not mean hard sessions. There is no threshold or race-pace work yet, because you first need to run longer before you run faster. The build is a gradual lengthening of the running blocks, with total time growing by roughly 10% a week at most. I will plan a lighter week around every fourth week so your legs can catch up.

If the weeks go as planned, that path gets you to running continuously well before Sun Nov 15. Smooth, steady weeks matter more than any single big session. I will adjust as I see how your effort and calves respond.
